name: Eta Aquariid Meteor Shower
description: Peak activity — up to 50 meteors per hour
tip: Best viewed after midnight, away from city lights

name: Summer Solstice
description: Longest day of the year in the Northern Hemisphere
tip: Great night to observe noctilucent clouds at high latitudes

name: Jupiter at Opposition
description: Jupiter is at its closest and brightest — magnitude -2.8
tip: Even binoculars will show Jupiter's four Galilean moons

name: Perseid Meteor Shower
description: Peak activity — up to 100 meteors per hour
tip: No equipment needed — find a dark spot and look northeast

name: Partial Lunar Eclipse
description: Moon passes through Earth's shadow — 94% coverage
tip: Visible with the naked eye — watch the shadow creep across the moon

name: Leonid Meteor Shower
description: Peak activity — up to 15 meteors per hour
tip: Best viewed in the pre-dawn hours facing east
